{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104.2","title":"catch-up 2: per-provider entitlement ranges (the participation-window MUST)","description":"docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §8, and the part the note says implementers will get wrong.

The hub must record, per room and per provider, the sequence ranges during which that provider had a participant. A catch-up answer is bounded by them: nothing from before its first participant joined, nothing from after its last left. Otherwise catch-up becomes a retroactive read of a room the provider was removed from, which is a worse hole than the one being closed.

This is the main NEW STATE the design needs. The hub already tracks the participant list and the Commits that change it; what it does not keep is the mapping from those changes to §4's sequences. Design that mapping before writing the serving code.

Tests, each showing a wrong provider is refused, as AGENTS.md requires of an authorization boundary: a provider that joined at sequence 500 is refused 1 to 499; one that left at 900 is refused 901 onward; one that was never a participant is refused everything; one that left and rejoined gets both of its ranges and not the gap between them.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:12:49.295632973Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T01:12:49.295632973Z","labels":["wg"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104.2","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:12:49.33191953Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"},{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104.2","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104.1","type":"blocks","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:13:15.899456919Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
new_value: {"notes":"Keyword downgraded: decision mimid-1wgh.107 (Mark, 2026-11-22) makes the participation-window bound a SHOULD, not a MUST -- a provider holds no MLS group keys, so a loose bound costs bandwidth and leaks metadata but never message content, and no peer can detect the violation. mimid still follows it. The practical effect on this bead is that the entitlement ranges are an efficiency and metadata-hygiene feature, not an authorization boundary that gates deploying .3: a conservative default (serve nothing before the provider's first join) is enough to start, and precision at the edges can be refined without an interop risk."}

{"notes":"DONE 2026-11-25.

THE DESIGN, and it is simpler than this bead imagined. The bead asked
for "the mapping from those changes to §4's sequences" -- from the
participant list and the Commits that change it onto fanout sequences.
That mapping is unnecessary. A provider is a destination of a fanout
EXACTLY when it had a member in the room (hub::submit::destinations), so
the window is written from the destination set, in the same transaction
that records the fanout.

Two things follow, and both are why this beats mapping the membership
changes:

* The ranges and the deliveries CANNOT DISAGREE. Catch-up can never
  serve a provider a sequence it was not originally sent, which is the
  property §8 is really about. Re-deriving the window from Commits
  would be a second answer to the same question, free to drift from the
  first -- and the drift would be undetectable, since §8 is a SHOULD no
  peer can check (decision mimid-1wgh.107).
* Presence is runs of CONSECUTIVE sequences, because between joining
  and leaving every fanout of the room reaches the provider. So a run
  is extended exactly when it ends at the previous sequence. This is
  why room_provider_range holds RUNS and not a first/last pair per
  provider: a pair would quietly serve the gap for a provider that left
  and rejoined.

Both are now in docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §8.3, where the note had
said this was "the part to design carefully before writing code", so
the next reader gets the conclusion and not the question.

WHAT SHIPPED.

* migrations/0019_participation_ranges.sql: room_provider_range
  (room_id, domain, first_seq, last_seq), keyed on (room, domain,
  first_seq), with an index on (room, domain, last_seq) for the
  extend-or-open lookup. Separate from room_event so retention pruning
  the events does not lose the window.
* store/log.rs record_participation: extends the run ending at
  fanout_seq - 1, else opens a new one with INSERT OR IGNORE so a
  replayed fanout cannot open a duplicate run. Called from
  insert_event per destination, so append_event, append_proposals and
  enqueue_fanout all record it.
* store/log.rs Store::provider_ranges and Store::serves: the runs, and
  the single question catch-up will ask.

TESTS, five, one per §8 rule, sharing one setup (a room whose fanouts
went to b.example throughout and to c.example at 3, 4 and 6). They were
one test first; split because a single failure masked the other four and
because the bead asked for tests per rule.

* a_provider_that_never_left_gets_every_sequence
* a_provider_is_refused_the_sequences_before_it_joined
* a_provider_is_refused_the_sequences_after_it_left
* a_provider_that_rejoined_gets_both_runs_and_not_the_gap
* a_provider_that_was_never_there_is_refused_everything

NOT IN SCOPE, and the thing not to misread:

1. NOTHING CALLS serves() YET. The window is recorded and queryable; no
   request path consults it, because there is no catch-up request path
   -- that is bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.3. So the bound is correct and is
   not enforced anywhere, which is the right order but should not be
   read as "the bound is in effect".
2. NOT ADDED TO AGENTS.md's AUTHORIZATION TABLE. This bead's
   description calls it an authorization boundary and cites the rule
   that each one needs a test showing a wrong identity is rejected. Its
   own notes downgrade it: decision mimid-1wgh.107 makes the bound a
   SHOULD, because a provider holds no MLS group keys, so a loose bound
   costs bandwidth and leaks metadata and never message content. The
   tests the description asked for are written; the table entry is not,
   because by .107 this is not one of its rows.
3. ROWS WITH fanout_seq 0 (events from before migration 0018) have no
   range, so they are unservable. Same as a pruned range, which .3 has
   to handle anyway."}

{"notes":"REVERSED 2026-11-25, the same day, by Mark: room_provider_range is
dropped (migrations/0022_drop_provider_ranges.sql). The delivered-fanout
table of bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.7 made it redundant, and Mark's unease
about accumulating tables of room membership is what surfaced it.

WHY IT WAS REDUNDANT. A room_fanout row exists for a (sequence, domain)
exactly when that provider was sent that fanout, so the rows answer
every question the runs answered: whether a provider was ever a
destination, the oldest it may ask for, the highest bounded to it, and
whether it left and rejoined -- the last exactly rather than in summary,
since a gap is an absent row. Store::fanout_window_for reads MIN and MAX
off those rows and replaces provider_ranges and serves.

I BUILT IT BEFORE THE TABLE THAT SUBSUMED IT, and said so: catch-up 2
landed before mimid-1wgh.37.104.7 existed as a question, and when I
built room_fanout I noticed the overlap and argued the two composed --
ranges for "is this in your window", rows for the bytes. They do not
compose; the rows answer both.

WHAT THE DROP COSTS, which my first argument for it understated. These
rows had NO retention, so for a provider whose fanouts are all pruned
they could still say "you were here for 100 to 200 and I hold from 500",
where the rows can only say "you have nothing here". Both are refusals,
so §5.1's MUST -- never a short answer that looks complete -- holds
either way, and a follower acts the same on both.

WHAT IT GAINS is that an unbounded table goes away: a row per provider
per membership run, for the life of the room, with nothing ever deleting
it. Against a §8 bound that decision mimid-1wgh.107 makes a SHOULD and
that no peer can detect, that is the worse of the two problems.

The §8 coverage is kept, through the authoritative mechanism:
the_window_a_provider_may_ask_about_comes_from_what_it_was_sent uses the
fixture the five deleted tests shared."}
